holidays.name: National Prime Rib Day
holidays.description: A day for carnivores to celebrate the slow-roasted, juicy, gloriously marbled cut of beef. Expect steakhouses to roll out the au jus and horseradish in tribute.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it grew out of restaurant and food-industry promotion and is listed on unofficial food holiday calendars. No single founder is clearly documented.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, prime rib doesn't have to be USDA Prime grade. The name comes from the 'primal rib' section of the cow, so a Choice-grade roast can still be called prime rib.

holidays.name: Morse Code Day
holidays.description: A day to tap out dots and dashes in honor of the code that once connected the world by telegraph. Fans send secret messages to friends, practice their SOS, and flash lights in rhythm.
holidays.origin: It is observed on the birthday of Samuel F. B. Morse, born April 27, 1791, who co-developed Morse code and helped popularize the electric telegraph.
holidays.funFact: The first long-distance telegraph message in 1844 was 'What hath God wrought,' sent from Washington, D.C. to Baltimore. Morse was also a successful painter before he turned to inventing.

holidays.name: Tell a Story Day
holidays.description: A day to put down the phone, gather around, and spin a yarn. Tall tales, family legends, and embarrassing childhood memories are all encouraged.
holidays.origin: It is a recurring unofficial observance promoted by storytelling and literacy enthusiasts, kept alive by libraries, teachers, and storytellers who like to share stories in person.
holidays.funFact: Studies of oral traditions suggest storytelling is as old as language itself. Some Aboriginal Australian stories appear to preserve memories of sea-level changes from over 7,000 years ago.

holidays.name: National Library Workers Day
holidays.description: A day for thanking the people who keep the books, quiet corners, and free Wi-Fi flowing. Patrons bring thank-you notes, snacks, and book puns for the hardworking librarians.
holidays.origin: It is observed during National Library Week in April and was launched by the American Library Association's Allied Professional Association to recognize library workers' contributions.
holidays.funFact: Modern libraries lend far more than books. Some let you borrow tools, board games, telescopes, and even fishing poles.

holidays.name: Sense of Smell Day
holidays.description: A day to stop and smell the roses, the coffee, and the bakery down the street. It's a chance to notice how much your nose shapes your memories and your meals.
holidays.origin: It grew out of sensory awareness and smell-loss advocacy efforts and is observed around the end of April on awareness calendars. Exact dates vary by source.
holidays.funFact: Smell is closely tied to memory because scent signals travel to the brain's emotion and memory centers. That is why a whiff of something can instantly teleport you back to childhood.
